status: Hypothetical accounting experiment. No Core replay, real battle validation, solver equivalence or deployment.

quantities.SP_q: 1q=0.25SP; unit stock in trace is q
quantities.equipment: 1E=one infantry-step equipment package, accounted internally in half-E

D.description: same-start no-investment control, not a fourth equal-spend main route

timing: T1..T16 German action-window convention, E1..E15 settlements only. New formation ordered before E_t has zero SP, participates in E_t maintenance, and becomes attack eligible at T(t+1) under assumed legal entry. No E16.
damage: Two initial one-step wounds; one fixed old-unit hit at start T3..T(H-1), cyclic ID. Hit on dead ID skipped and logged via actualBattleLoss. H16 main. Repair oldest recoverable wound, then form one unit if materials suffice. Initial-wound waiting excluded from mean.
attack: All alive non-resting units each get at most one hypothetical independent target; no movement cost for infantry. Full means paid 1SP and debt factor 1. Reduced/zero stock attacks remain possible. Sum of unit attack opportunities is not verified Core attack-command count.
recovery: Select at most one alive wounded unit with D<2 and sufficient equipment/personnel. Assume this selected unit starts in legal recovery position, does not attack or move. No map legality proof.
supply: Single corridor, quarter-SP deterministic water filling to common maintenance level first, then lowest reserves to cap; tie rotation by insertion order and t modulo living roster. Equipment freight reserves net maintenance capacity first. This is not the actual multi-route optimizer.
salvage: Each lost infantry step has 0.5E recoverable wreck and 0.5E written off. Wreck remains unavailable equipment until repaired; C consumes up to0.5E wreck each E>=3 into local equipment, without another long-haul freight. No personnel refund.
